question: At its core, how does a language model write its reply?

options.text: By copying the closest answer from a database
By searching the live web for text
By predicting one likely next token at a time
By following a fixed script written by humans

teachLine: It builds a reply one token at a time, each time guessing what word-piece most plausibly comes next. String enough good guesses together and you get a sentence.
callbackFact: A language model generates text autoregressively, predicting the next token step by step, rather than retrieving stored answers or running a fixed script.
